definition: Job rotation is a workplace practice in which workers are moved between different job tasks or roles. In this context, it is used as an intervention to help reduce work-related problems such as musculoskeletal strain.

reasons: The packet supports job rotation only as one of several intervention measures for work-related musculoskeletal disorder; it does not define job rotation as moving workers between different tasks or roles.

The claim that it is used to reduce work-related problems such as musculoskeletal strain is broader and more specific than the source, which only says it is an intervention to address underlying issues in bank workers with musculoskeletal disorder.
The packet only mentions “job rotation” as an example of an intervention; it does not define job rotation as a workplace practice that moves workers between different job tasks or roles.

The definition’s specific wording (“reduce work-related problems such as musculoskeletal strain”) is only partially supported: the packet refers to work-related musculoskeletal disorder, but does not use the term “musculoskeletal strain” or clearly state that job rotation reduces it.
